dct_description_sm: We wish to recognize and thank the literally thousands of Costa Rican and international people, experiences, and institutions that have contributed and continue their thinking and support for the content of this work. We are especially grateful for the staff and institutions that have created and maintained ACG since the beginning of its existence in 1966 and full germination in 1985. Without that, these ideas and reality would not exist, nor would there be the opportunity to notice what is happening to its biodiversity.
Caterpillar diet breadth in Area de Conservación Guanacaste (ACG), a large and diverse Neotropical wildland in northwestern Costa Rica: toxins, silica, aluminium, and sclerophylly.
